title: TDDR Rising Narratives — Friday evening, Nov 20
summary: A snapshot of opposition narratives from the Right and the Far Left as of 5:20 PM ET Friday, Nov 20, 2026. Built for TDDR (Too Dumb Didn't Read). The biggest mover today is new on the Right: Mayor Zohran Mamdani's plan to close Rikers Island by 2032. The Rikers query matched 37,350 posts in 24 hours, 37,252 of them from 7 AM to 5 PM ET versus 78 the same hours Thursday, and 'Rikers' was trending in the U.S. The Right's frame is that shrinking the jail population to 4,100 means 'letting criminals out'; the plan sets a 2032 population target through diversion and faster cases, closing Rikers has been city law since 2019, and the new timeline still needs City Council approval. The 'nullify the midterms' push cooled but stayed second (8,970 posts, 2.73×), still made of copy-paste demands to the White House; the president has no power to cancel results. A $4.1 trillion CRFB estimate for House Democrats' 100-day agenda nearly quadrupled daytime tax-hike posts (1,150 versus 302). On the Far Left, the Senate's failed Iran war powers vote (51-48) pushed the 'Jeffries won't defund the war' frame up (1,603 posts; 809 in daytime versus 547), and Van Hollen vs. Schumer rose in daytime posts (1,884 versus 1,551) as Sen. Angela Alsobrooks's vote for Schumer circulated. The resurfaced 2023 'We stand with Israel' clip, the impeachment card and the reparations card all cooled. Two faded cards were dropped: 'AIPAC Shakur' and the Jeffries/AIPAC petition. Every count, quote and fact-check comes from sources and X queries pulled this evening or carried over from this morning and labeled. Nothing here is invented.

trends.detail: U.S. trends were pulled at about 5:07 PM ET with x.get_trends_by_woeid (WOEID 23424977, max 50; 50 returned). Sports (Daniel Jones, 36,462 posts; Colts, 57,750; Bayern), WhatsApp (111,024), 'Riemann Hypothesis' (29,502) and holiday movies (Home Alone, 27,295) dominated. 'Rikers' (44,035 posts) matches Mayor Mamdani's plan to close the jail complex, so the Rikers card received the trend bonus; it is the only scored card that did. '#AccountabilityIsComing' (1,573 posts) is a pro-Democratic hashtag about investigations in the new Congress, not an opposition narrative, so we did not score it. 'Vance and Rubio' had no post count in the trend object and we did not review it. 'Transgender Day of Remembrance' (20,346) and the market trends ('Nasdaq,' 37,288; 'S&P 500,' 21,106) are not opposition narratives. Where a trend object had no tweet_count, its volume is unavailable and we did not estimate it.

oppositionNote.body: Right = narratives the Right is pushing after the Democratic midterm wave. Far Left = pressure on Democratic leadership and the incoming majority from the party's left. Tonight's top card is a Right attack on a Democratic mayor, not on Congress: we include it because Mamdani is being used as the national face of the party, and the frame ('Democrats let criminals out') is aimed at Democrats everywhere. The Iran-funding and Van Hollen cards are tagged Far Left because the pressure on Jeffries and Schumer comes from the party's left, even though some posts come from 'America First' accounts too. The Social Security card stays tagged Right because the 'Ponzi scheme' frame is a Right talking point, even though many posts matching it are backlash. The tag is the primary opposition frame.

methodology: Last updated Friday, Nov 20, 2026, 5:20 PM ET. This is a research snapshot for TDDR, not a live API, and it will go stale overnight. U.S. X trends were pulled at about 5:07 PM ET. This morning's snapshot (Nov 20, 7:25 AM ET) is kept in the archive and was not overwritten. Fourteen of its sixteen narratives were re-counted with the same queries so momentum compares like with like. The new 24-hour window overlaps this morning's by 14 hours (5 PM Thursday to 7 AM Friday ET), so we also report each query's 7 AM–5 PM ET Friday count against the same hours Thursday. Two narratives were dropped because they faded: 'AIPAC Shakur' (1,109 posts in the last 24 hours, 0.59× its prior daily average; 416 from 7 AM to 5 PM versus 2,057 the same hours Thursday) and the Jeffries/AIPAC petition (159 posts, 0.09×; 64 versus 480). One was added with a new query: Mayor Mamdani's Rikers closure plan. Other candidates were counted and not carved out as cards: frustration that Democrats are already talking about needing 60 Senate votes, after Neera Tanden urged a filibuster-proof majority in 2028 (1,520 posts, 0.80×; 725 from 7 AM to 5 PM versus 508), noted here; the '$4.1 trillion' figure on its own (80 posts), noted on the tax card; and Mamdani's pitch for monthly NYC-DSA donations (125 posts), noted on the DSA card.

For each narrative we ran one English-language X search with x.get_posts_counts_recent at hourly granularity over a 167-hour window from 6:00 PM ET Friday, Nov 13, through 5:00 PM ET Friday, Nov 20. The last 24 hourly buckets (5:00 PM ET Thursday, Nov 19, through 5:00 PM ET Friday, Nov 20, exactly 24 hours) give the 24-hour count, and the whole window gives the 'seven-day' total. We counted named news or fact-check outlets whose coverage we opened or retrieved in this evening's searches and cite on the card. Official government pages, bill text, advocacy groups, research groups, budget watchdogs, congressional committees, blogs, X News summaries, and X posts are cited as sources but not counted as outlets. We re-researched the Rikers, Van Hollen, Iran-funding and tax cards and counted only outlets retrieved this evening on those cards, which is why some outlet counts changed. We pulled fresh post samples for the 'nullify' and Social Security cards but did not re-count their coverage, so their outlet counts are carried over. For the other cards, which we did not re-research this evening, the outlet count is carried over from this morning, and each of those cards says so. We noted whether each topic appeared on the U.S. trends list at about 5:07 PM ET.

Score = 50% volume index + 30% acceleration index + 20% coverage index. Volume index is 100 × log10(1 + last-24h posts) / log10(1 + the highest last-24h count in this set). Acceleration index is 100 × min(last-24h / prior daily average, 3) / 3, so a triple-or-higher average scores 100. Prior daily average is (seven-day total − last 24h) / 6. Coverage index is 70 × min(outlets, 7) / 7, plus 30 if the topic was on the U.S. X trends list this evening. Only the Rikers card got the trend bonus this evening. The Rikers and Erie queries had almost no baseline earlier in the week, so their acceleration indices are maxed out. The Van Hollen, popular-vote compact and rigged-midterms queries carry last week's spikes in their seven-day totals, which keeps their acceleration low even though daytime volume rose. Read the post counts alongside the scores. Morning-to-evening score changes also reflect the much higher volume ceiling (37,350 this evening versus 9,580 this morning), which lowers every other card's volume index, and how much coverage we retrieved.

Counts are query matches, not unique posts or unique users, and queries can overlap. The 'nullify' query overlaps the rigged-midterms query. The Israel-video, Jeffries Iran funding and DSA queries share many speaker-race posts. The Rikers query requires 'Rikers' plus a closure, release or Mamdani term, so it also catches straight news posts and rebuttals. The Social Security query also catches posts attacking Johnson. The immigration query includes the phrase 'Stephen A' with Democrats/immigration terms, so it can catch unrelated Stephen A. Smith posts. The Erie query includes the bare word 'Erie' with citizenship or voting terms, so it can catch unrelated Erie posts. The impeachment query also catches Democrats discussing impeachment. The rigged-midterms query also catches posts mocking fraud claims. The tax query catches generic complaints about state taxes. Replies are included, and automated @grok replies make up a visible share of several queries. Sentiment is a qualitative label from relevancy-sorted post samples and from quotes in news coverage, not a scientific poll. This evening we pulled fresh samples for the Rikers, 'nullify,' Van Hollen, Iran-funding, Social Security and tax queries. Other cards carry this morning's sentiment and say so. Daily bar charts use UTC days (a UTC day starts at 7:00 PM ET the previous evening). Bars marked * are partial windows. Hourly charts are labeled in ET.

disinfo.caveatBody: New this evening: 'Mamdani is releasing thousands of criminals' (posts cite 2,100, 2,500 or 7,000) is misleading: the plan sets a target of no more than 4,100 people in custody by the end of 2032, reached through diversion, supervised release and shorter case delays, and Rikers stays open until borough jails are built (City of New York; Gothamist). Closing Rikers is not Mamdani's invention; a 2019 City Council law required it, and his plan moves the deadline later and still needs Council approval (AP). Whether the target can be met safely is a fair debate, which New York Post opinion writers dispute. 'Democrats' agenda is a $4.1 trillion tax hike' mixes up costs and taxes: CRFB's $4.1 trillion is a ten-year cost estimate, and its largest piece is repealing tariffs, which lowers taxes. The 'nullify the midterms' demand is still circulating; the president has no authority to cancel state results or declare martial law (Brennan Center; Protect Democracy), and fact-checkers found no evidence that machines switched votes. Carried over from this morning: the 'We stand with Israel' clip is real but from Nov. 14, 2023 (AP); posts using the Ian Murray case as proof that noncitizens are voting have no evidence behind them; 'The Protect Our Neighbors Act gives 1.6 million people green cards' is misleading; 'Democrats are already preparing a third impeachment' is a prediction by Jim Jordan, not a report; CNBC's experts say the 'Ponzi scheme' label misses how Social Security is funded, and PolitiFact has rated the comparison False when others made it; 'Pressley's H.R. 40 pays reparations' is misleading; 'Democrats are importing voters' runs into the law, since noncitizens cannot vote in federal elections; 'Jeffries backs the Iran war' is false as stated; 'Democrats will defund the military to shut down the government' is misleading; and Lead Stories found no '30,000-case' Texas voter fraud probe.

'Rikers' was on the U.S. X trends list at about 5:07 PM ET (44,035 posts). On Friday Mayor Zohran Mamdani released the city's first strategic plan to close Rikers Island: the island's jails would be emptied by Dec. 31, 2032, as four borough jails open (Brooklyn in 2029, the Bronx and Queens in 2031, Manhattan in 2032), and the jail population would fall from about 6,600 to no more than 4,100 through diversion, supervised release and shorter case delays (City of New York; Gothamist). The new deadlines need City Council approval (AP). Closing Rikers is not new: a 2019 City Council law set the original 2027 target, which Gothamist says slipped after years of delays. The Right's frame is that shrinking the population means releasing dangerous people: a New York Post opinion piece says the plan would put 'more than 1,000 violent criminals back on the streets,' and posts cite 2,100, 2,500 or 7,000 releases. The query also catches straight news posts and rebuttals, so read the count as attention, not agreement.
talkingPoints: Mamdani is closing Rikers and letting thousands of criminals out.
You can't cut the jail population by 2,500 without releasing people charged with violent crimes.
First he cut the NYPD's protest unit, now he empties the jails.
This is what a Democratic socialist city looks like — and Democrats want it everywhere.
narratives.amplifiers: Right: New York Post opinion pages ('more than 1,000 violent criminals back on the streets'; 'barely begins to face reality'), @JoeLange (13,175 views), @clerpatriot, @DKH013, @Bubblebathgirl, @MichaelARothman and @Influenze1 ('Socialists love to release or cut deals with criminals'). News coverage: AP, POLITICO and Gothamist. Supporters of closing Rikers include progressive groups and the Vera Institute, which interviewed the city's Close Rikers czar, Dana Kaplan.
narratives.whyItWorks: Crime and disorder are the Right's most reliable attack on big-city Democrats, and Mamdani is the most visible democratic socialist in office, so a jail story in New York becomes a national preview of 'Democratic rule.' Specific-sounding numbers (2,100, 2,500, 7,000) turn a six-year population target into an image of open cell doors. It also pairs with other Mamdani stories circulating Friday, such as his NYPD unit cut and his pitch for monthly DSA donations, to build a single picture.
narratives.audience: Outer-borough and suburban New Yorkers worried about crime, national conservative audiences who see Mamdani as the face of the Democratic left, and police and corrections-officer communities.
narratives.counter: Nobody is opening the doors on Friday. The plan sets a population target for the end of 2032, reached through diversion, supervised release and faster cases, and Rikers stays open until the borough jails are built (City of New York; Gothamist). Closing Rikers has been city law since 2019, passed under de Blasio; this plan actually pushes the deadline later, and it still needs City Council approval (AP). Take the real question seriously: critics doubt the target can be met safely, so answer with how many people are held on lower-level charges and how case delays will be cut, not with slogans.

Florida attorney Peter Ticktin, lead counsel for convicted former Colorado clerk Tina Peters and a friend of Trump's from New York Military Academy, called on Trump to declare the 2026 state and federal results void, invoke the Insurrection Act, which he said would bring martial law, and act before the new Congress is seated on Jan. 3; he urged supporters to call the White House. talkingPoints: The 2026 midterms were rigged by algorithms.

Invoke the Insurrection Act; call the White House and demand it.

narratives.amplifiers: Right: The Gateway Pundit (@gatewaypundit, 89,762 views on its post), @DavidJHarrisJr (16,632 views), @GailGolec, @jimhoft_, and many small accounts posting identical 'BREAKING' copy and the White House switchboard number. Origin: attorney Peter Ticktin (@PeterTicktin). Election-skeptic allies Tina Peters and Mike Lindell have pushed related federal-intervention ideas (MS NOW).
narratives.whyItWorks: It gives voters who cannot accept a blue wave a deadline (Jan. 3), a remedy (one presidential order) and a task (call the White House), which turns grievance into action. It comes from someone with real access: Ticktin says he knows Trump from their teens and has been in the Oval Office with Peters (MS NOW). And it builds on months of vote-switching rumors that fact-checkers have already debunked but that many in the audience never saw corrected.
narratives.audience: Hard-core 'stolen election' believers, Tina Peters supporters, Gateway Pundit and Telegram/Gab audiences, and older conservative voters primed by the 2020 fight.
narratives.counter: Say it plainly and calmly: the president has no power to cancel state election results, and no law lets him declare martial law (Brennan Center; Protect Democracy). The Insurrection Act lets troops help enforce the law, not overturn it, and federal law bars troops at polling places. On 'algorithms': Snopes, PolitiFact and FactCheck.org found no evidence that machines switched votes in the 2026 midterms; the reports traced to touchscreen errors that voters could correct. Point out that Republicans won races on the same machines. Don't amplify the phone-number campaign.

factChecks.claim: The president can nullify the 2026 midterm results and declare martial law.
factChecks.detail: The Constitution gives the president no power over how states run or certify elections, and no statute authorizes martial law. The Insurrection Act permits troop deployments to enforce the law, not to change results, and federal law bars armed federal officers at the polls. This row relies on legal analyses from the Brennan Center and Protect Democracy; it is not a rating from a fact-check outlet.

factChecks.claim: Voting machines switched votes in the 2026 midterms.
factChecks.detail: Snopes found no evidence machines switched votes in either direction during the 2026 midterms; the reports it reviewed likely reflected human error or touchscreen alignment problems, and voters can review selections before casting. PolitiFact and FactCheck.org reached similar conclusions in October. Ticktin's specific 'algorithm' claim was not separately rated.

talkingPoints: Two weeks after an election about grocery prices, it's 'reparations now.'
Reparations first, groceries never.
Their 'Majority Priorities' list is reparations, abolish ICE and Medicare for All.
They'll pass it, Trump vetoes it, then they call him racist.

narratives.amplifiers: Right: @gatewaypundit (7,276 views) and its many reposts; @DailySignal; @Milajoy (172 likes, 3,754 views); Fox News. Pressley's office posted the agenda video.
narratives.whyItWorks: It gives the Right a single word that reframes the whole Democratic wave as racial redistribution, and it lands on the exact message Democrats won on (affordability). A ranked list with reparations at the top is easy to screenshot, and it shifts the debate from what Democrats will pass to what the Left wants.
narratives.audience: Conservative and MAGA-aligned voters, white working-class swing voters who respond to 'race-based' framing, and Right media audiences (Fox News, Leading Report). Texans remain a secondary audience for the SB 376 thread.
narratives.counter: Say what H.R. 40 is: a study commission with no payments, which has sat in committee for nearly two years. It is one member's priority list, not the caucus agenda; Jeffries and the new leadership team are leading with costs. Don't litigate reparations itself on the Right's terms; pivot to what the majority will bring to the floor first.

factChecks.claim: Pressley's H.R. 40 would pay reparations to Black Americans.
factChecks.rating: Misleading — it creates a study commission
factChecks.detail: DC News Line reports H.R. 40 would set up a 15-member commission to study slavery and later discrimination and recommend remedies, authorizes $20 million for the commission, and would not itself pay anyone. Pressley filed no new bill with her post; H.R. 40 has seen no action since it was referred to committee on Jan. 3, 2025. This is TDDR's read of that reporting, not a rating from a fact-check outlet.

factChecks.claim: Pressley forced a House floor vote on reparations.
factChecks.detail: Her post called for Democrats to pass reparations and other priorities with their majority. Fox News and DC News Line report a priorities list, not a scheduled vote, and the new majority does not take power until January. This is TDDR's read of that reporting, not a rating from a fact-check outlet.
factChecks.outlet: Fox News / DC News Line (TDDR read)

factChecks.claim: Texas Democrats filed a bill to pay reparations and build a genealogy database of all state residents.
factChecks.detail: SB 376's text creates a bureau that maintains a database 'for the purpose of assisting residents of this state in establishing ancestral ties with freedmen,' issues ID cards to residents who establish those ties, and provides legal help filing reparations claims. It does not appropriate reparations payments or require every resident to be traced. The bill is prefiled, not passed, and a 2025 version died in committee. This is TDDR's read of the bill text, not a rating from a fact-check outlet.

No red lines means no accountability. Why push someone who backs Jeffries?

narratives.counter: Be accurate about what passed: one chapter urged a run, which is not an endorsement, and Ocasio-Cortez has said she'll decide after the midterms. On red lines, ask what specific commitments the chapter wants and how it will hold its members to them.
